item.title: fm-cli is in the official Omarchy package repo
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: I have been waiting on this one. fm-cli, my little terminal client for Fastmail, is now an optional package in the official Omarchy repo. It is not on the default install, which is fine: it is there if you want it, and it is not in anyone’s way if you don’t.
item.content:encoded:
I have been waiting on this one. fm-cli, my little terminal client for Fastmail, is now an optional package in the official Omarchy repo. It is not on the default install, which is fine: it is there if you want it, and it is not in anyone’s way if you don’t.

On Omarchy, open the menu with Super + Space, choose Install > Package, and type fm-cli. Or, from a terminal:

omarchy pkg add fm-cli

Then sign in with fm-cli auth login, which opens Fastmail’s consent page in your browser. That is it.

fm-cli is a small Go client for Fastmail’s JMAP API. It gives you a full-screen mail app in the terminal, commands that print JSON, a live watch over Fastmail’s push connection, and offline reading and drafting. It is also the engine behind the Fastmail plugin for Omarchy.

The package that landed today is 0.3.3. Newer releases, up to 0.3.6, are on GitHub and still installable with mise if you want the latest. I’ll work on getting the official package caught up.

If you are not on Omarchy, the usual options are still there: mise, autonomix-cli, and the .deb, .rpm and tarball releases.

https://fm-cli.ninepointlabs.com/

https://github.com/ninepointlabs/fm-cli

item.title: Comms: all-in-one text chat for WoW Forever
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: Comms is a new, free addon for World of Warcraft: Forever that does text chat: one addon instead of five. If you’d rather type than use voice, it’s meant to make chat quicker and easier. Version 0.1.0 is out, the first release.
item.content:encoded:
Comms is a new, free addon for World of Warcraft: Forever that does text chat: one addon instead of five. If you’d rather type than use voice, it’s meant to make chat quicker and easier. Version 0.1.0 is out, the first release.

What it does

  • Easier to read: class-coloured names, short channel names ([2. Trade] becomes [2. T], and you can edit them) and timestamps.
  • Links: URLs become clickable (click to copy). When someone asks for an invite in whispers, party, raid or guild, an [invite] link appears, and Alt-click on a name invites them.
  • Alerts: your name and your keywords play a sound, flash the tab and land in an Alerts list.
  • Whispers: one window with a tab per person (Battle.net friends too), unread badges and a reply box. History is kept for every character.
  • History: chat is kept across /reload and logout, and /comms search finds old lines. Up and Down recall what you typed, no Alt needed.
  • A bigger chat box with Tab completion for names, commands and channels.
  • Channels: it can leave or hide General, Trade, Services and friends for you, account-wide.
  • Quick lines: ten editable lines like inv pls or ty for the group! on a quick-bar or key bindings, and /tt whispers your target.

It steps back in instances

Forever locks chat down for addons in dungeons, raids and battlegrounds. There, Comms never sends anything itself, and quick lines go into the chat box for you to press Enter.

Get it

On Linux, OmaForge installs it and keeps it updated:

omaforge install -c forever github:ninepointlabs/comms

On any other system, download Comms-v0.1.0.zip from the v0.1.0 release, unzip it into _forever_/Interface/AddOns/, then type /reload and /comms. It’s for WoW Forever only. This Comms is by Nine Point Labs and isn’t related to Forever Comms Voice, Guild Comms, Group Comms or Quick Comms. The source is on GitHub. It’s an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard. Questions go to help@ninepointlabs.com.

item.title: Tazu's Addon 0.2: Dwarf Shamans, world PvP and two smart buttons
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: Tazu’s Addon, the free Shaman companion for World of Warcraft: Forever, just reached 0.2.0. It started out for Horde Shamans. This release brings in the Alliance’s Dwarf Shamans, adds a PvP mode for world PvP, and puts two new buttons on the Shaman bar.
item.content:encoded:
Tazu’s Addon, the free Shaman companion for World of Warcraft: Forever, just reached 0.2.0. It started out for Horde Shamans. This release brings in the Alliance’s Dwarf Shamans, adds a PvP mode for world PvP, and puts two new buttons on the Shaman bar.

Dwarf Shamans and the Alliance

The addon now reads your race and faction. A Dwarf Shaman gets their own leveling path (Coldridge Valley, Dun Morogh, Loch Modan, the Wetlands, then zone ranges up to 60), the Alliance Shaman trainers, the Dwarf versions of the totem quests and Dwarf lessons. Orc and Troll Shamans keep their Horde path, and neither side sees the other’s.

Dwarves also get a Stoneform hint. It lights up when a Poison, Disease or Bleed is on you, but only when the game lets the addon read your debuffs. When it can’t, it stays quiet instead of guessing.

PvP mode

Turn it on per profile with /tazu pvp. You get a World PvP priority list for each spec, PvP totem picks (Grounding against casters, Tremor against fear, Earthbind to kite), and a new Learn › PvP page with tips. On a PvP-ruleset realm the addon suggests PvP mode once. It never turns it on by itself.

Two new buttons and totem sets

  • Smart Shock: Earth Shock by default, Frost Shock while you hold Shift (or Ctrl or Alt, your choice in Settings) once you know it.
  • Smart Heal: Healing Wave on your friendly target, or on you when you have none. Alt casts Lesser Healing Wave once you know it. It always uses your highest rank.
  • Totem sets: a saved PvE set and PvP set for each profile. Keep the guide’s pick or pin your own totem for each element in Settings › Shaman bar, and the Totems hint switches sets along with PvP mode.

The new buttons work like the old ones: no keys are bound by default, one key press is one cast, and they only change out of combat.

Get it

On Linux, OmaForge picks up the update with omaforge update -c forever, or installs it fresh:

omaforge install -c forever github:ninepointlabs/tazus-addon

On any other system, download TazusAddon-v0.2.0.zip from the v0.2.0 release, unzip it into _forever_/Interface/AddOns/, then type /reload. It’s for WoW Forever only. The source is on GitHub. It’s an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard. Questions go to help@ninepointlabs.com.

item.title: Repokase 0.2.6: sturdier, and now as .deb, .rpm and Flatpak
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: Repokase, the desktop app that puts all your GitHub repositories on one counter, is out in version 0.2.6. It copes better when something on your machine goes wrong, and it now installs the usual way on far more Linux distributions. The code is on GitHub.
item.content:encoded:
Repokase, the desktop app that puts all your GitHub repositories on one counter, is out in version 0.2.6. It copes better when something on your machine goes wrong, and it now installs the usual way on far more Linux distributions. The code is on GitHub.

New packages

Next to the Arch package and the AppImage, every release now ships a .deb, an .rpm and a self-hosted Flatpak bundle. Like the AppImage, they carry their own Python and Qt, so they work on Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora and openSUSE. In the Flatpak, Repokase follows your desktop’s light or dark setting rather than an Omarchy theme.

Sturdier

  • A damaged cache no longer stops it starting. Repokase moves a broken cache file aside (nothing is deleted), builds a fresh one and tells you where the old file went. If the cache can’t be written at all, for example because of folder permissions, a window says so instead of nothing happening.
  • Sign in without a keyring. With no GNOME Keyring or KWallet available, you can still sign in. Your token is kept in memory for that session only, never on disk, and About shows where your sign-in actually lives.
  • The sidebar fits, so counts are no longer cut off, and Ctrl+B and Ctrl+1 go back to the automatic layout when toggled back.
  • The AppImage’s --remove-desktop-entry only removes what --install-desktop-entry added, and installing never overwrites desktop files or icons from somewhere else.

Get it

Download the package for your system from the 0.2.6 release (every file has a .sha256 next to it). On Arch or Omarchy:

sudo pacman -U https://github.com/ninepointlabs/repokase/releases/download/v0.2.6/repokase-0.2.6-1-any.pkg.tar.zst

Or with autonomix-cli: autonomix-cli add https://github.com/ninepointlabs/repokase. Please report anything odd on the issue tracker.

item.title: Goodbye Persistwise web, hello Persistwise Desktop
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: Persistwise is now a free, open source desktop app for Linux. It keeps a full copy of every page you save, offline, with no account and no Persistwise servers.
item.content:encoded:
Persistwise on the web has closed. To everyone who signed up, tried it, sent a note or told a friend: thank you. The idea hasn’t gone anywhere, though. Today it moves onto your own computer as Persistwise Desktop, a personal web archive with no account and no Persistwise servers. Version 0.1.0 is out now, it’s free on Linux, and the code is MIT licensed on GitHub.

What it does

  • Save any page. Paste a link and Persistwise keeps a full copy, with the text, styles, images, icons and fonts packed into one file that opens offline. Scripts are stripped out, and PDFs and other files are kept exactly as downloaded.
  • Watch your feeds. Follow a blog, newsletter or social feed (RSS, Atom or JSON Feed), and every new post is saved automatically.
  • Browse and search offline. Everything you’ve saved is searchable, even with no network.
  • Wayback Machine backup. Pages are also sent to the Internet Archive’s Save Page Now. It’s on by default and easy to turn off, and if it’s busy, your local copy is never affected.
  • IPFS, if you want it. Pin to your own IPFS node or with your own Pinata key. It’s off by default.
  • Your data stays with you. Everything lives in a folder on your computer, and there’s no telemetry.

Why the change

The web version needed an account, our servers and a subscription. The desktop app needs none of those: the copies live on your own computer, and the optional Wayback and IPFS backups go straight from your machine to services you choose. Wayback snapshots made by the web version are kept by the Internet Archive, so they stay right where they are.

Bring your web data over

If you had a Persistwise web account, email help@ninepointlabs.com and we’ll send your export. Then choose Import from Persistwise web in the app, or run:

persistwise-desktop --import persistwise-export.zip

Your feeds, posts, Wayback and IPFS links and saved copies come over, and the app carries on checking your feeds. Importing a fresher export later updates what changed, with no duplicates.

Get it

Version 0.1.0 runs on any 64-bit Linux. The v0.1.0 release has an AppImage, a self-hosted Flatpak bundle, a .deb (Ubuntu 22.04 or newer), an .rpm for Fedora and openSUSE, and an Arch package with its PKGBUILD, each with a SHA-256 checksum. On Omarchy, or anywhere you use autonomix-cli:

autonomix-cli add https://github.com/ninepointlabs/persistwise-desktop

A Windows version through the Microsoft Store is planned. Questions and bug reports are welcome at help@ninepointlabs.com or on the issue tracker.

item.title: omaforge 0.2.10: big voice-over packs update again
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: omaforge is the World of Warcraft addon manager for Linux and Omarchy. Version 0.2.10 lets you choose how large an addon download can be, so big voice-over packs update again.
item.content:encoded:
omaforge is the World of Warcraft addon manager for Linux and Omarchy. Version 0.2.10 lets you choose how large an addon download can be, so big voice-over packs update again.

What’s new

Large addons update again. Voice-over packs such as Spoken Audio now ship archives over 500 MiB, and omaforge used to refuse them with “download larger than 536870912 bytes”. The default limit is now 2048 MiB, so those packs install and update normally.

Set your own limit. Settings → Network has a new “Skip addon downloads larger than … MiB” field. You can also set max_size_mb under [downloads] in ~/.config/omaforge/config.toml. An archive may unpack to up to four times that size, which keeps the guard against oversized archives in place.

Clearer errors. When an addon goes over the limit, the message now tells you what the limit is and where to change it.

Get it

  • Arch / Omarchy: sudo pacman -U omaforge-0.2.10-1-any.pkg.tar.zst, then omaforge setup omarchy
  • Debian 13+ / Ubuntu 26.04+: sudo apt install ./omaforge_0.2.10-1_all.deb
  • Fedora: sudo dnf install ./omaforge-0.2.10-1.noarch.rpm
  • Any other Linux: the AppImage, chmod +x omaforge-0.2.10-x86_64.AppImage && ./omaforge-0.2.10-x86_64.AppImage. Add --install-desktop-entry to put it in your app menu.
  • With autonomix-cli: autonomix-cli add https://github.com/ninepointlabs/omaforge

The packages are on the v0.2.10 release, and the source is on GitHub.

item.title: Bahá’í Reader 1.1: Study your own books, and keep your notes in step
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: Bahá’í Reader 1.1 adds Study: import PDFs of your own, such as your copies of Ruhi Institute books, then highlight, take notes and type your answers right on the workbook’s blank lines. Your notes can now be backed up and kept in step between devices through a sync folder.
item.content:encoded:
Bahá’í Reader has a new section. Version 1.1 adds Study, a place to study PDFs of your own, such as your copies of Ruhi Institute books. Two bug-fix releases, 1.1.1 and 1.1.2, followed the same evening after the first real study session on a phone and a desktop.

The app includes no Ruhi Institute material and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Ruhi Institute. A PDF you import is copied into the app on your device. It is never uploaded anywhere, and the app still goes online only to download a language when you ask.

Study

Study is a sidebar section on the desktop and a tab on phones. Import a PDF (Ctrl+O on the computer, or “Open with” or Share on Android), and then:

  • Answer on the page. Type your answers on the workbook’s blank lines. The app finds the lines for you, and Tab moves to the next blank. You can also put an answer in a box anywhere on the page.
  • Highlight in five colours, write notes on highlights, bookmark pages, write notes about the book, search inside it, and pick up where you stopped.
  • Each time through a book is kept on its own. Start a new time through (“1st time, Nov 2026”, “2nd time…”) and it begins empty. Earlier ones stay read-only, so you can see your earlier answer beside each question or compare two times side by side.
  • Organize and find. File books in categories, and search every highlight, note and answer you’ve written.
  • Export to Markdown, one time through or all of them, ready for Obsidian.
  • A table of contents for PDFs that don’t have one (new in 1.1.1). The app builds it once from the book’s headings and keeps it on your device.

If you import another edition of a book you’ve already marked up, the app recognizes it and offers to move your marks across. Anything it can’t find is listed so you can place it yourself.

On Linux, Study can also bring in your Dogear marks for a book you import, answers included. 1.1.2 fixes Dogear answers that began on the question’s own line and were drawn over the printed words.

Your notes, everywhere you study

Study made one thing more urgent: notes you write on the phone at a study circle should also be there on the laptop at home.

  • Settings → Back up or move your notes exports everything you’ve made to one file and merges that file on another device.
  • Sync through a folder keeps your notes in step between devices through a folder that Syncthing, Dropbox or the like shares. The app itself never goes online. Your sync program carries the files. Since 1.1.1, imported PDFs travel through that folder too, so a book imported on one device opens on the others. A switch in Settings turns that off.
  • Saved → Highlights & notes now gathers everything in one place, across the Writings, the prayers and Study, with a search and a Markdown export.

Other changes

  • Highlights come in five colours: yellow, green, blue, pink and purple. Older magenta highlights are now pink and look the same.
  • On phones, Today, Writings, Prayers and Study sit in a bottom bar.
  • Your highlights, notes and saved passages now live in a small database beside the settings file. The first start of 1.1 moves them there and keeps a copy of the old settings file.
  • On Android, imported books are never included in Android’s backup, and a switch in Settings decides whether your notes are.
  • 1.1.1 fixes typing answers: Space no longer turns the page, and single-key shortcuts go to the text while you’re typing an answer, a note or a search.

Get it

Bahá’í Reader 1.1.2 is out for Linux, Windows and Android. Downloads are on bahaireader.org and the GitHub releases page. The Windows build isn’t code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn you: choose More info, then Run anyway. On Linux, autonomix-cli keeps it up to date:

autonomix-cli add https://github.com/ninepointlabs/bahai-reader
autonomix-cli install bahai-reader
# or, if you already track it:
autonomix-cli update

The source is on GitHub. The code is MIT licensed; the bundled texts have their own attribution in DATA-NOTICE.md. This is a free, independent community app, not an official publication of a Bahá’í institution.

item.title: The Terminal List: a watch list for WoW Forever
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: The Terminal List is new: a free, open source addon for World of Warcraft: Forever that keeps a personal watch list of players who crossed you, were rude, or don’t play nice. It works on both factions, and version 0.1.0 came out today. The code is on GitHub.
item.content:encoded:
The Terminal List is new: a free, open source addon for World of Warcraft: Forever that keeps a personal watch list of players who crossed you, were rude, or don’t play nice. It works on both factions, and version 0.1.0 came out today. The code is on GitHub.

Who’s on the list

You decide. Type /tlist add with a name (or with a player targeted), right-click their portrait or their name in chat, or open the list window with /tlist. The window lets you search, filter, sort and add a note to each entry, so you remember why someone is there.

The list is shared by every character on your account and stored only on your computer. Nothing is uploaded or shared with anyone.

Open-world PvP, and only that

If another player kills you in the open world, they’re added to the list, or their kill count goes up if they’re already on it. Battlegrounds, arenas, dungeons, raids, other instances and duels never count, so the PvP you sign up for doesn’t fill your list.

Forever doesn’t always tell addons who landed the killing blow. When it doesn’t, The Terminal List asks you about the hostile player you were fighting instead of guessing.

Spot them again

Listed players are easy to recognize the next time you meet:

  • a red crosshair beside their nameplate and on the target frame,
  • a line in their tooltip with your note and kill count,
  • a crosshair on their lines in chat,
  • and an optional once-per-session alert when one shows up (off by default).

Get it

On Linux, OmaForge installs it and keeps it updated:

omaforge install -c forever github:ninepointlabs/the-terminal-list

On any other system, download TheTerminalList-v0.1.0.zip from the v0.1.0 release, unzip it into _forever_/Interface/AddOns/, type /reload, then /tlist. It’s for WoW Forever only. It hasn’t been tested in game yet, so please report anything odd on the issue tracker. It’s an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard. Questions go to help@ninepointlabs.com.

item.title: Forever Rogue: a do-everything Rogue companion for WoW Forever
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: Forever Rogue is new: a free, open source Rogue companion for World of Warcraft: Forever. It works for every Rogue race and both factions, and it was built around Rip, a Human Rogue of the Alliance who started out in Northshire Valley. Version 0.1.0 came out today, and 0.1.1 followed shortly after with pickpocket spots on the minimap.
item.content:encoded:
Forever Rogue is new: a free, open source Rogue companion for World of Warcraft: Forever. It works for every Rogue race and both factions, and it was built around Rip, a Human Rogue of the Alliance who started out in Northshire Valley. Version 0.1.0 came out today, and 0.1.1 followed shortly after with pickpocket spots on the minimap.

It’s the fifth of the family, after Andric’s Addon for Priests, Parzelle’s Addon for Mages, Tristan’s Addon for Paladins and Tazu’s Addon for Shamans, so the window will feel familiar if you’ve used any of them.

Pockets, boxes and locks

A Rogue’s coin comes from other people’s pockets, so that’s where Forever Rogue starts. Type /frogue.

  • Pick Pocket log: every pickpocket with its coin, items, junkbox tier, mob, level and zone. You get totals for the session, the day and your lifetime, copper per pickpocket, pickpockets per hour, your best mobs, and a refill timer per mob so you know when a pocket is worth trying again.
  • Best targets: pickpocket spots by level and zone. Your own results sit next to community data from GoldScout players, shown with sample sizes and marked unconfirmed.
  • Minimap pins (new in 0.1.1): pins for spots near your level that the research has map coordinates for, plus every spot where you’ve picked a pocket yourself. Hover one for the mob, your earnings there and the distance. Spots without sourced coordinates get no pin; nothing is guessed. Turn them off with /frogue pins.
  • Junkboxes and Lockpicking: the boxes in your bags and bank, whether you can open them, and what they’re worth, using Auctionator prices when it’s installed and vendor prices otherwise. There’s also a lockpicking route and the locked dungeon doors.

Poisons and the Rogue bar

Poisons shows what’s on each weapon (in Forever a poison and a sharpening stone can share one), your stock, and the suggested poison for each hand. The Rogue bar has a Pick Lock button that opens the next box you can, main-hand and off-hand poison buttons, reagent counts and a pocket counter. One press is one action, out of combat only, and no keys are bound by default.

Everything else a Rogue needs

  • Rotation: Solo, Dungeon and Raid priorities for Assassination, Combat and Subtlety, using only spells you know.
  • Talents: seven Icy Veins builds laid out on Forever’s own Rogue trees, each exactly 51 points.
  • Gear and bags: upgrades for your level, plus the next bag upgrade for your race and faction.
  • Leveling: a path, trainer visits and the class quests for your race and faction.
  • Gold: each session broken down by source, from pickpocket coin to quests.
  • PvP: honor and rank where the game lets addons read it, battlegrounds, Rogue PvP notes and poison choices.
  • Learn the Rogue, plus reminders for poisons, reagents, Thieves’ Tools and class quests.

Forever doesn’t give addons the combat log and hides some values in combat. Inside dungeons it hides mob names too, so those pickpockets are logged as “unknown mob”. When something can’t be read, the addon says so instead of guessing.

Get it

On Linux, OmaForge installs it and keeps it updated:

omaforge install -c forever github:ninepointlabs/forever-rogue

On any other system, download ForeverRogue-v0.1.1.zip from the v0.1.1 release, unzip it into _forever_/Interface/AddOns/, type /reload, then /frogue. It’s for WoW Forever only, and it hasn’t been tested in game yet, so please report anything odd (especially pins that don’t line up with the minimap) on the issue tracker. Every fact carries its source and the date it was checked. It’s an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard. Questions go to help@ninepointlabs.com.

item.title: Bahá’í Reader for everyone: rebuilt with Flutter
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: Bahá’í Reader is rebuilt with Flutter, so the same offline prayer book and Writings reader now runs on Linux, Windows and Android. We’re still Omarchy users, but this app is meant for anyone who needs it.
item.content:encoded:
Bahá’í Reader, the offline prayer book and Writings reader, started out as a GTK app for Linux. We’ve rebuilt it with Flutter, so the same reader now runs on Linux, Windows and Android. Version 1.0 is the first release of the new app.

Why Flutter

Let’s get one thing out of the way: we’re still Omarchy users. Most of what we make at Nine Point Labs is built for Linux and Omarchy first, and that isn’t changing.

Bahá’í Reader is a little different. A prayer book is something you reach for on whatever is in front of you: the family laptop, a phone at a devotional gathering, the computer at work. The people who could use it aren’t all running Linux, and an app full of prayers and the Writings should be shared with whoever needs it. Flutter lets us keep one codebase and ship it to many platforms, so a fix or a new feature reaches everyone at once.

Same reader, new home

Before switching, we listed every feature of the GTK app and worked through them one by one, so the move wouldn’t cost anyone the things they rely on. What you know is still here:

  • Offline, and private. English is bundled. Other languages download only when you ask, and nothing else ever uses the network. No accounts, no analytics, no telemetry.
  • The library and search. Writings grouped by book, prayers grouped by category, and a search that ignores accents and apostrophes, so “Bahaullah” finds “Bahá’u’lláh”.
  • Highlights, notes and saved passages, plus Copy with citation.
  • Today and the obligatory prayers. The Badí‘ date (changing at sunset), sun times for your city, your obligatory prayer’s window with a private “Said today”, the next Feast and Holy Day, the Fast, the passage of the day and the Alláh-u-Abhá counter.
  • Light, Dark and Sepia, and on Omarchy it still follows your live theme.

If you used the GTK app on Linux, the first start brings over your highlights, notes, saved passages, collections, reading places and settings. The old app’s files are only read, never changed, so nothing is lost if you go back.

Where it runs today

  • Linux, where we use it every day: the .deb, .rpm, Arch/Omarchy package, AppImage and Flatpak bundle are all there, or install it with autonomix-cli.
  • Windows (64-bit): an installer that doesn’t need administrator rights, or a zip. Last night I tested it on Windows myself, and it works well. It isn’t code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn you the first time; choose More info, then Run anyway. Reminders aren’t sent on Windows yet.
  • Android (7 and up, phones and tablets): an APK you install from the download page. The phone opens on a Today tab, and reminders arrive even with the app closed.

What’s left: macOS and iOS

The Flutter project already has the starting pieces for macOS and iOS, but neither has been built or tested. Building for Apple platforms needs a Mac, and we don’t have one yet. When we get one, macOS and iOS are next. Until then we’d rather say “not yet” than ship something we haven’t tried.

Get it

Downloads for every platform are on bahaireader.org and the GitHub releases page. On Linux, autonomix-cli keeps it up to date:

autonomix-cli add https://github.com/ninepointlabs/bahai-reader
autonomix-cli install bahai-reader
# or, if you already track it:
autonomix-cli update

The source is on GitHub. The code is MIT licensed; the texts and translations are not, and DATA-NOTICE.md has the details. This is a free, independent community app, not an official publication of a Bahá’í institution.

Thank you to everyone who has prayed, read and studied with Bahá’í Reader so far. It’s a joy to be able to share it with more people.

item.title: Tazu's Addon: a do-everything Shaman companion for WoW Forever
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: Tazu’s Addon is new: a free, open source Shaman companion for World of Warcraft: Forever. It knows Elemental, Enhancement and Restoration, has dual spec from day one, and is named for Tazu, a Troll Shaman of the Horde who started out in the Valley of Trials today. Version 0.1.0 is out, the first release.
item.content:encoded:
Tazu’s Addon is new: a free, open source Shaman companion for World of Warcraft: Forever. It knows Elemental, Enhancement and Restoration, has dual spec from day one, and is named for Tazu, a Troll Shaman of the Horde who started out in the Valley of Trials today. Version 0.1.0 is out, the first release.

It’s the fourth of the family, after Andric’s Addon for Priests, Parzelle’s Addon for Mages and Tristan’s Addon for Paladins, so the window will feel familiar if you’ve used any of them.

One window for the whole Shaman

Type /tazu (or /shaman). Home shows what your trainer has now and next, your riding savings, your next totem class quest, and anything that needs attention: no weapon imbue, no Lightning or Water Shield, totems not down in a fight, Ghost Wolf waiting to be trained.

  • Rotation: Solo, Dungeon and Raid priorities for each spec, using only spells you know, with a next-spell helper that tracks Maelstrom Weapon stacks, your own cooldowns and procs, mana tips and a post-fight summary.
  • Gear: For my level, Best overall and By bracket views, how to get each item with a map pin, tooltip upgrade lines weighted for your spec and a glow on bag upgrades. Enhancement advice follows Blizzard’s Nov 10/11 hotfix.
  • Leveling: a Horde Troll path through Durotar and the Barrens, trainer visits, riding and gold, and the totem class quests: Call of Earth at 4, Fire at 10, Water at 20, Air at 30, then The Tempest’s Weapons.
  • Talents: builds drawn on Forever’s own Shaman trees, each checked to add up to exactly 51 points at level 60.
  • Learn the Shaman: every spell and talent, totems, imbues, shields, group role and level-by-level lessons.
  • Dual spec: two profiles per character. The suggested plan is to level as Enhancement, then at 40 run Enhancement plus Restoration for groups.

The Shaman bar

The weapon imbue button puts the right imbue for your spec on your weapon at the highest rank you know, in one press, and shows how long is left: Windfury from level 30, Rockbiter before that. The Fire Nova button lights up only while one of your Fire totems is down, since in Forever Fire Nova erupts from your current Fire totem. Beside them, a Shield hint and a Totems hint suggest the right shield and one totem per element for Solo, Dungeon or Raid.

The bar works alongside Blizzard’s own totem tracker and Call of the Elements bar rather than replacing them. Forever doesn’t give addons the combat log and hides some values in combat, so when something can’t be read, the addon says “hidden” instead of guessing. Everything is advice: one key press is one cast, nothing casts by itself, and no keys are bound by default.

Get it

On Linux, OmaForge installs it and keeps it updated:

omaforge install -c forever github:ninepointlabs/tazus-addon

On any other system, download TazusAddon-v0.1.0.zip from the v0.1.0 release, unzip it into _forever_/Interface/AddOns/, type /reload, then /tazu. It’s for WoW Forever only. Every fact carries its source (Blizzard first, then Icy Veins and Wowhead) and the date it was checked. The source is on GitHub. It’s an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard. Questions go to help@ninepointlabs.com.

item.title: Tristan's Addon: a do-everything Paladin companion for WoW Forever, with PvP
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: Tristan’s Addon is new: a free, open source Paladin companion for World of Warcraft: Forever. It knows Holy, Protection and Retribution, has dual spec from day one, and adds something its siblings don’t have: a real Battle section for PvP. Version 0.1.0 is out, the first release.
item.content:encoded:
Tristan’s Addon is new: a free, open source Paladin companion for World of Warcraft: Forever. It knows Holy, Protection and Retribution, has dual spec from day one, and adds something its siblings don’t have: a real Battle section for PvP. Version 0.1.0 is out, the first release.

It’s the third of the family, after Andric’s Addon for Priests and Parzelle’s Addon for Mages, so the window will feel familiar if you’ve used either one.

One window for the whole Paladin

Type /tristan (or /paladin). Home shows what your trainer has now and next, your riding savings, your next class quest, and anything that needs attention: no Blessing on you, no Aura, no Seal in melee range, Righteous Fury on while you’re not tanking.

  • Rotation: Solo, Dungeon and Raid priorities for each spec, using only spells you know, with a small next-spell helper, a post-fight summary with mana tips, and a Seals & auras tab.
  • Gear: upgrade lines in tooltips weighted for your spec, a glow on bag upgrades, how to get each item with a map pin, and a PvP weights toggle that puts Stamina first.
  • Leveling and talents: zones, dungeons, trainer visits and class quests, plus builds drawn on Forever’s own Paladin trees. Every level-60 build is checked to add up to exactly 51 points, PvP builds included.
  • Learn the Paladin: every spell and talent, how Seals and Judgement work in Forever, group etiquette, common mistakes and a PvP basics track.
  • Dual spec: two profiles per character. The suggested plan is to level as Retribution, then at 40 run Retribution plus Holy for battlegrounds.

The Paladin bar

The Blessing button blesses the next friendly player missing your Blessing, one press at a time: you first, then your group nearest-first, your target, then friendly nameplates. It picks Might for Warriors, Rogues and Hunters, Wisdom for casters and healers, or Kings for everyone if you choose it, and you can override any class. Beside it, an Aura hint and a Seal hint suggest the right one for what you’re doing.

Battle: PvP in the same window

Tristan Ludlowe lives on a PvP realm, so the addon has a Battle group with six tabs:

  • Honor & Rank: your rank and Honor where the client lets addons read them, and the next rank reward.
  • Battlegrounds: Warsong Gulch, Arathi Basin, Darkspear Islands and Alterac Valley, with the objective, your spec’s role and where to queue. Only brackets your level allows are lit.
  • PvP bar: one-press buttons for Freedom, Cleanse, Blessing of Protection, Hammer of Justice and Repentance.
  • Cooldowns with a Forbearance timer, a Burst coach that follows your own casts and lights the next step, and World PvP status for your zone with survival tips for leveling on a PvP realm.

Forever doesn’t give addons the combat log, and other players’ health and casts are hidden from addons in combat. So Tristan’s Addon doesn’t track enemy trinkets, diminishing returns or enemy players, and it says so plainly instead of pretending. Everything is advice: one key press is one cast, and nothing casts by itself.

Also new: Parzelle’s Addon 0.1.1

The Mage companion got two buttons beside its Conjure Button. Arcane Intellect buffs the next person who needs it, skipping Warriors and Rogues. Hand out opens a trade with your target or the next group member (lowest mana first) and fills it with the best rank of water and food they can use, with food only for Warriors and Rogues. You still click the final Trade yourself.

Get it

On Linux, OmaForge installs it and keeps it updated:

omaforge install -c forever github:ninepointlabs/tristans-addon

On any other system, download TristansAddon-v0.1.0.zip from the v0.1.0 release, unzip it into _forever_/Interface/AddOns/, and type /reload. It’s for WoW Forever only. Every fact carries its source (Blizzard first, then Icy Veins and Wowhead) and the date it was checked. The source is on GitHub. It’s an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard. Questions go to help@ninepointlabs.com.

item.title: folderblog 0.2.11: posts ordered by date and time
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: folderblog 0.2.11 puts posts in order by date and time, so several posts on the same day finally show up in the right order. The home page, archives, tag pages, feeds and the podcast list are all newest first by it.
item.content:encoded:
folderblog 0.2.11 puts posts in order by date and time, so several posts on the same day finally show up in the right order. The home page, archives, tag pages, feeds and the podcast list are all newest first by it.

How it works

Every post date now carries a time of day. To set the time yourself, write it in date:

date: 2026-11-10 09:28

A full timestamp with an offset works too, like date: 2026-11-10T09:28:00-06:00.

A post with only a day (a 2026-11-10- filename or date: 2026-11-10) gets the time it was first committed to git, or else the file’s modified time. That time is saved in dates.toml the first time the post is published, so editing it later never reshuffles the day. The day, and so every address, stays the same.

You can also set a timezone in blog.toml:

timezone = "America/Chicago"

Dates written without an offset are read in that zone. Without it, folderblog uses the computer’s own zone, as before.

A couple of other details:

  • Friendlier date typos. An unreadable date is now a warning (and the filename’s date is used) when the filename has one. folderblog check also warns about an unreadable updated.

Read this before you update

  • timezone needs 0.2.11 or newer. Older versions refuse a blog.toml that has it, so update every machine that builds the blog first.
  • Expect a one-time change to dates.toml. The first build adds a time for each post dated by filename or a date-only date:. Commit it with your blog.
  • Feeds now show real times instead of midnight, and a few same-day posts may swap places in the feed.

Grab it

SystemCommand
Arch / Omarchysudo pacman -U folderblog-bin-0.2.11-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst
Debian / Ubuntusudo apt install ./folderblog_0.2.11-1_amd64.deb
Fedora / RHEL / openSUSEsudo dnf install ./folderblog-0.2.11-1.x86_64.rpm
autonomix-cliautonomix-cli add https://github.com/ninepointlabs/folderblog

Already installed? Install the new package, then run systemctl --user restart folderblog. The packages and a plain tarball are on the v0.2.11 release, and the source is on GitHub.

item.title: Parzelle's Addon: a do-everything Mage companion for WoW Forever
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: Parzelle’s Addon is new: a free, open source Mage companion for World of Warcraft: Forever. Pick Arcane, Fire or Frost, and one window tells you what to cast, what to wear, where to quest, what to train and where you can teleport, all for your spec and your level. Version 0.1.0 is out today, the first release.
item.content:encoded:
Parzelle’s Addon is new: a free, open source Mage companion for World of Warcraft: Forever. Pick Arcane, Fire or Frost, and one window tells you what to cast, what to wear, where to quest, what to train and where you can teleport, all for your spec and your level. Version 0.1.0 is out today, the first release.

It’s built on the same window as Andric’s Addon, the Priest companion, so if you’ve used that one you already know your way around.

One window, built around what to do next

Type /parzelle (or /mage) and start on Home. It shows what your trainer has for you, your savings toward riding, your next Mage class quest, and anything that needs attention: missing buffs, conjured food and water running low, upgrades sitting in your bags, news you haven’t read. A search box finds any spell, talent, item, quest or dungeon.

  • Rotation: Solo, Dungeon and Raid priorities for each spec, plus Crowd control and Mana tabs. It shows only spells you can cast at your level, offers an optional on-screen helper, and posts a short summary with a mana tip after each fight. It only advises; nothing is cast for you.
  • Polymorph tracker: the helper shows who you sheeped and how long it has left, warns if it breaks early, and keeps Frost Nova, Counterspell and Cone of Cold cooldowns beside it.
  • Gear: tooltips say whether an item is an upgrade for your spec, counting only the spell school that spec uses. Upgrades glow in your bags, and a click shows who drops an item, which quest rewards it or how it’s crafted, with a map pin.
  • Leveling and talents: trainer visits, zones and dungeons for your level and faction, class quests, riding and gold goals, and recommended builds drawn on Forever’s own talent trees. Frost is marked as the safest spec to level with.
  • Learn the Mage: 44 short lessons that unlock as you level, plus 49 spells and 36 talents explained.
  • Dual spec: each character gets two profiles, and the addon switches with you when you swap specs.

The Conjure Button and the travel bar

A small Conjure Button shows how much conjured water, food and mana gem you’re carrying. Each press makes whatever you’re shortest on: a mana gem if you have none, then water up to your target, then food. It casts the highest rank you know, and you can set the targets and bind it to any key in Settings.

Portals & teleports lists every teleport and portal for your faction, the level you learn it, and your reagent counts. A separate travel bar holds one button for each one you know. Both keep Blizzard’s rules: one press, one cast, set up out of combat, no macros.

It shows its sources

Every fact keeps its source (Blizzard, Icy Veins and Wowhead) and the date it was checked. Where the sources disagree or say nothing yet, such as which reagents Forever’s portals still need, the names of Forever’s conjured food and water, or raid gear before the raids open on December 9, the addon says so instead of guessing. A What’s new page collects Forever and Mage changes, and new releases bring updated research.

The addon is named for Parzelle Starfall, a High Order Skyborne Mage who started out on Zephras Isle and hadn’t picked a spec by level 8. It’s built for her and tested on her.

Get it

On Linux, OmaForge installs it and keeps it updated:

omaforge install -c forever github:ninepointlabs/parzelles-addon

On any other system, download ParzellesAddon-v0.1.0.zip from the v0.1.0 release, extract it into _forever_/Interface/AddOns/, and type /reload. It’s for WoW Forever only; Classic Era and retail won’t load it. The source is on GitHub. It’s an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard. Questions go to help@ninepointlabs.com.

item.title: Bahá’í Reader 0.1.9: the official bahai.org texts, offline
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: Bahá’í Reader, the offline prayer book and Writings reader for Linux, now reads from the source. Version 0.1.9 brings the official texts of the Bahá’í Reference Library at bahai.org into the English library, adds two big collections that weren’t in the app before, and makes the window happy at phone-like sizes.
item.content:encoded:
Bahá’í Reader, the offline prayer book and Writings reader for Linux, now reads from the source. Version 0.1.9 brings the official texts of the Bahá’í Reference Library at bahai.org into the English library, adds two big collections that weren’t in the app before, and makes the window happy at phone-like sizes.

The official text, wherever bahai.org has it

The English books and prayers now show bahai.org’s own text wherever bahai.org publishes the same passage. That covers the Hidden Words, Gleanings, Prayers and Meditations, Tablets of Bahá’u’lláh, the Kitáb-i-Íqán, the Kitáb-i-Aqdas, the Epistle to the Son of the Wolf, Some Answered Questions, Days of Remembrance, and 455 of the 472 prayers. bahai.org’s numbering, footnotes, diacritics and italics come along with it.

A prayer taken from a bahai.org book now names that book in its citation, so Copy with citation points to where the text really came from. The Riḍván messages also show the official text now; eight that bahai.org dates differently (Naw-Rúz and other dates) moved to Messages of the Universal House of Justice under their bahai.org dates.

Your saved passages, collections and reading position keep working. Every passage kept its place, so nothing you saved points at the wrong text.

New in Writings

  • 515 messages of the Universal House of Justice, every one bahai.org lists, grouped by decade.
  • Seven works of Shoghi Effendi: The Advent of Divine Justice, Bahá’í Administration, Citadel of Faith, God Passes By, The Promised Day Is Come, The World Order of Bahá’u’lláh and This Decisive Hour, with their footnotes and headings.
  • Group by book or by author, from the list above the search box. By author lists Bahá’u’lláh, ‘Abdu’l‑Bahá, Shoghi Effendi and the Universal House of Justice, then their books.

All of it is bundled with the app. Bahá’í Reader still doesn’t connect to bahai.org, or anywhere else, to read.

Narrow windows and easier navigation

Below 700 pixels wide, the contents list and the reading pane take turns instead of squeezing together, and the window can shrink to 320 pixels. Passages now show headings like “Arabic no. 1” or “Paragraph 4”, with your position (“1 of 71”) between Previous and Next. Neither pane can be dragged so small that it disappears.

Get it

autonomix-cli add https://github.com/ninepointlabs/bahai-reader
autonomix-cli install bahai-reader
# or, if you already track it:
autonomix-cli update

The .deb, .rpm, .pkg.tar.zst, AppImage and Flatpak are on the v0.1.9 release, and the source is on GitHub. The bahai.org texts carry “Copyright © Bahá’í International Community” and aren’t covered by the app’s MIT license; DATA-NOTICE.md has the details. This is an independent community app.

item.title: Dogear 0.1.3: EPUB books, marked up like a PDF
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: Dogear is the reader for studying, made for Omarchy. Version 0.1.3 opens EPUB books, so it now reads, highlights and remembers your PDFs and EPUBs.
item.content:encoded:
Dogear is the reader for studying, made for Omarchy. Version 0.1.3 opens EPUB books, so it now reads, highlights and remembers your PDFs and EPUBs.

EPUB books

Open an .epub the same way as a PDF: from the Open dialog, the command line, by dropping it on the window, or from the library. The first time, Dogear sets the book in pages (6 × 9 in, chapters starting on a new page), which takes a second or two for a long book, and keeps those pages. After that everything works as it does for a PDF: highlights in five colors, notes, bookmarks, answer lines, search, the library and the Markdown export. The Contents panel shows the book’s own table of contents.

Your marks belong to the book

The library lists the EPUB, and the EPUB is what Dogear copies into Library/. The laid-out pages live in your library folder, so they sync with your marks and another computer shows the same pages. They’re never laid out again, so your marks stay on the words you marked. Another copy of the same book (same identifier, such as its ISBN) is offered your marks, just as with PDFs.

Good to know

  • Books get one plain, readable style. Bold, italics, headings, lists, tables and images are kept; the publisher’s styling, links inside the book and most SVG drawings aren’t.
  • DRM-protected EPUBs can’t be opened.
  • There’s no choice of page size or font yet.
  • Fix: the Arch package now depends on qt6-svg. Without it, Dogear’s icon (and SVG images in books) couldn’t be shown. Most desktops already have it, so few noticed.

Get it

autonomix-cli add https://github.com/ninepointlabs/dogear
autonomix-cli install dogear
# or, if you already track it:
autonomix-cli update

On Arch or Omarchy you can also grab dogear-0.1.3-1-any.pkg.tar.zst and run sudo pacman -U on it; on any other Linux, the AppImage runs as is. Both are on the v0.1.3 release, and the source is on GitHub. Questions go to help@ninepointlabs.com.

item.title: omaforge 0.2.9: star addons to find them later
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: omaforge is the World of Warcraft addon manager for Linux and Omarchy. Version 0.2.9 lets you star addons, so you can bookmark one you haven’t installed and come back to it later.
item.content:encoded:
omaforge is the World of Warcraft addon manager for Linux and Omarchy. Version 0.2.9 lets you star addons, so you can bookmark one you haven’t installed and come back to it later.

What’s new

Star any addon. Click the ☆ on an addon in Explore, Search or Installed, or in its details view. Stars are saved between sessions, are shared by all your game versions, and stay when you remove the addon. An addon with no known source can’t be starred.

A new Starred tab. It sits between Search and Backups and lists everything you’ve starred, with a filter, a sort (Recently starred or Name) and a Not installed toggle. Install adds the addon to the game version selected in the sidebar, and if an addon has no build for that version you get the usual “no stable release” message.

Shortcut change. Ctrl+4 now opens Starred, and Backups moved to Ctrl+5.

Get it

  • Arch / Omarchy: sudo pacman -U omaforge-0.2.9-1-any.pkg.tar.zst, then omaforge setup omarchy
  • Debian 13+ / Ubuntu 26.04+: sudo apt install ./omaforge_0.2.9-1_all.deb
  • Fedora: sudo dnf install ./omaforge-0.2.9-1.noarch.rpm
  • Any other Linux: the AppImage, chmod +x omaforge-0.2.9-x86_64.AppImage && ./omaforge-0.2.9-x86_64.AppImage. Add --install-desktop-entry to put it in your app menu.
  • With autonomix-cli: autonomix-cli add https://github.com/ninepointlabs/omaforge

The packages are on the v0.2.9 release, and the source is on GitHub.

item.title: Bahá’í Reader 0.1.8: a Today view for the Badí‘ day
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: Bahá’í Reader, the offline prayer book and Writings reader for Linux, now has a place to start the day. Version 0.1.8 adds a Today view that gathers the Badí‘ date, the sun, your obligatory prayer, the next Feast and Holy Day, the Fast and the passage of the day on one page. Everything is worked out on your machine; nothing is looked up online.
item.content:encoded:
Bahá’í Reader, the offline prayer book and Writings reader for Linux, now has a place to start the day. Version 0.1.8 adds a Today view that gathers the Badí‘ date, the sun, your obligatory prayer, the next Feast and Holy Day, the Fast and the passage of the day on one page. Everything is worked out on your machine; nothing is looked up online.

Today

Today is the new first entry in the sidebar. It shows the Badí‘ date, sunrise, noon and sunset, when your obligatory prayer falls, the next Feast and Holy Day, the Fast, and the passage of the day as a card. In the sidebar it also lists the next twelve months and this year’s months.

New installs open on Today. If you already use the app, it keeps your place. Ctrl+T and the Today button now open this view instead of jumping straight to the passage of the day, which lives on the page as a card.

Badí‘ dates come from the Universal House of Justice’s table for 172 to 221 B.E. Past that, the app says the dates haven’t been published yet rather than guessing.

Location, kept on your machine

Sun times need a place. Type a city and it’s found offline in a bundled GeoNames list, or enter coordinates yourself. Your location is never detected and never sent anywhere.

Where days and nights vary greatly, Clock times lets you enter the hours your National Spiritual Assembly uses, and those replace the sun. The app has no clock times of its own.

Obligatory prayer, the counter and the Fast

  • Prayer times and Said today: the times come from the bundled texts, and you can mark the prayer as said. For the Long Obligatory Prayer you choose which twenty-four hours count, because no text says and no ruling has been made. Sunset to sunset is the default.
  • Alláh-u-Abhá counter (Ctrl+Shift+A), shown with Kitáb-i-Aqdas ¶18.
  • The Fast: the day, the fasting hours, and an optional private Fasted today check.

Reminders, off until you want them

Reminders cover the obligatory prayer, Feasts, Holy Days and the Fast. They’re all off by default. If you turn them on, you can also opt in to keep them running when the window is closed.

A tidier header

The Aa menu now holds only reading settings. Languages & offline libraries and About moved to a new ⋮ menu, alongside Location & reminders and Keyboard shortcuts. F1 still opens About.

Get it

autonomix-cli add https://github.com/ninepointlabs/bahai-reader
autonomix-cli install bahai-reader
# or, if you already track it:
autonomix-cli update

The .deb, .rpm, .pkg.tar.zst, AppImage and Flatpak are on the v0.1.8 release, and the source is on GitHub. This is an independent community app; the texts keep their own attribution in DATA-NOTICE.md.

item.title: Sunsetting Rune, and why I'm writing in WordCraft now
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: Rune is archived. WordCraft does what Rune set out to do and more, it’s open source, and it runs on Linux, so I’d rather point you there than compete with it.
item.content:encoded:
Earlier this month I started building Rune, a word processor for Linux and Omarchy with AI built right into the writing surface. Today I’m archiving it, and I’d like to tell you why.

Why I built Rune

Word processors on Linux felt like a choice between heavyweight ports and plain text editors pretending to be word processors. And every one of them treated AI as a sidebar plugin. I wanted the opposite: a fast, native app where the model is part of the page, where you can ask it to fix a paragraph and the fix lands right in your document as one undo step.

Rune got further than I expected. It went from an idea to version 0.8.7 in about two weeks, with packages for Arch, Debian and Fedora, an AppImage for most other distros, headers and footers, tables, and sign-in for ChatGPT and OpenRouter.

What I learned

Quite a lot, honestly. Rune started on LibreOfficeKit and ended up as a single Qt process that reads and writes ODF itself, because the first design had a performance ceiling I couldn’t get past. Along the way I learned to test real files instead of trusting documentation. That habit caught a bug in Qt’s own ODF writer, where a table right after a list silently disappeared when LibreOffice opened the file. By the end, Rune was checked by 504 automated tests. I’ll carry that way of working into everything I build next.

Then I found WordCraft

Recently I came across WordCraft, a fast, open-source word processor written in Rust by the ArtCraft team. I tried it, and it’s really good.

It does what Rune set out to do, and more. It has a ribbon and styles, works with .docx natively along with .odt, Markdown and more, exports PDF, and has track changes and comments, offline spelling and grammar, footnotes, a table of contents, and citations in APA, MLA, Chicago and IEEE. It runs on Linux as a Flatpak, plus macOS, Windows, FreeBSD and the web.

The part that really got me is how it treats AI. Its commands are available through a command-line tool, a JSON control channel and an MCP server, so AI assistants can work inside your documents. That’s the idea I was chasing with Rune, done in a more open way: you bring whichever assistant you like.

It’s still in development, but it’s already well past where Rune is.

Why archive instead of compete

I could keep going. But I’m one person, word processors are a lot of work to maintain, and the world doesn’t need two small open-source editors chasing the same idea when one of them is already further along. I’d rather spend my time on things only Nine Point Labs can build, and send you to the better tool.

So Rune is archived. The code stays up under the MIT license, along with the existing releases, if you’d like to learn from it or fork it. The README now points to WordCraft.

Give WordCraft a try

If you write on Linux, or anywhere really, please give WordCraft a try. The source is on GitHub if you’d like to dig in or help out.

Thank you to everyone who tried Rune or sent a kind word about it. It meant a lot.

item.title: StoryTracker takes its own screenshots now
item.dc:creator: Tim
item.description: StoryTracker is the World of Warcraft addon that keeps a record of your character’s adventures: quests, zones, levels, deaths, bosses, loot and more. It comes in two versions, one for WoW Forever and one for Retail. Yesterday’s releases (Forever 1.0.4 and 1.0.5, Retail 1.1.3 to 1.1.5) add automatic screenshots at the moments that make a good story, and make the addon easier to install with an addon manager.
item.content:encoded:
StoryTracker is the World of Warcraft addon that keeps a record of your character’s adventures: quests, zones, levels, deaths, bosses, loot and more. It comes in two versions, one for WoW Forever and one for Retail. Yesterday’s releases (Forever 1.0.4 and 1.0.5, Retail 1.1.3 to 1.1.5) add automatic screenshots at the moments that make a good story, and make the addon easier to install with an addon manager.

Screenshots at story moments

StoryTracker now takes a screenshot about three quarters of a second after:

  • a quest turn-in
  • a level up
  • an achievement (on Forever, only if the client fires the achievement event)
  • a boss kill
  • your first visit to a zone
  • other story moments, such as entering a dungeon or battleground, a battleground result, rare or elite kills, a new mount, epic or better loot, duels, joining a guild, a reputation standing going up, and deaths

There’s also an optional timed shot every 15 minutes, taken only when you’re out of combat, not on a loading screen and not AFK.

It takes at most one shot every 20 seconds. When two moments land together, like a turn-in that also dings, the shot is labelled with the bigger one. If you turn on “hide UI”, the interface is hidden for the shot while you’re out of combat, and it’s never touched in combat.

Each shot is logged in the addon’s saved data with its time, the file name WoW gives it, what happened, the zone and subzone, and your character’s name, realm and level. Log entries older than 30 days are dropped. Addons can’t delete files, so StoryTracker never removes screenshots itself; clean up the game’s Screenshots folder outside the game.

Turning it on and off

Screenshots are on by default, and everything is under /storytracker shots:

  • /storytracker shots on|off turns automatic screenshots on or off.
  • /storytracker shots <event> on|off controls each kind: quest, levelup, achievement, boss, newzone and story.
  • /storytracker shots timer on|off|<minutes> sets the timed shot (1 to 120 minutes, 15 by default).
  • /storytracker shots hideui on|off hides the interface for out-of-combat shots (off by default).
  • /storytracker shots log shows the last few logged shots.

Easier installs with an addon manager

Each release is now built with the BigWigs packager and comes with a small release.json file that says which game it’s for. Addon managers such as OmaForge use it to install the right StoryTracker for each client, so the Forever build goes to Forever and the Retail build goes to Retail. Installed copies also link back to their GitHub page now. Retail 1.1.5 updates the addon for the 12.1.5 client so it isn’t flagged as out of date.

Why it matters

StoryTracker’s notes are what turn a play session into a post on My Azeroth Life. Words were only half of it. Now each story moment comes with a picture taken right when it happened, and the log says exactly which shot goes with which moment, so a post can show the boss kill or the first look at a new zone instead of a stock image.

Privacy

Nothing changes here. StoryTracker has no network access, since WoW addons can’t use the internet. Screenshots are saved by WoW to its own Screenshots folder on your computer, and the log only records when and where each one was taken.

Download the latest Forever release or Retail release, or install it with OmaForge. The code is on GitHub for Forever and Retail.
